issues.legal_issue: A grant of probate does not determine ownership of property or bar a civil suit seeking a declaration of title and injunction based on claims that the property belongs to a joint family.
material_facts: Probate had been granted for a will bequeathing the disputed properties, and that grant had been affirmed on appeal.
The civil suit alleged that the properties were joint Hindu family properties and that properties had been acquired using income from ancestral agricultural land.
The suit sought a declaration of title and an injunction against alienation; the lower courts dismissed it solely because probate had been granted.
issues.conclusion: The probate grant did not make the civil suit legally unmaintainable. The dismissal was set aside, and the suit was remitted for decision after issues were framed and evidence considered.
issues.legal_principle: A probate court determines whether the will was duly executed and attested and whether the testator had a sound disposing mind; it does not determine the testator’s title to the property or whether the property was joint ancestral or individually acquired. Probate conclusively establishes the will’s due execution and the executor’s legal character, but does not decide title. The civil court may admit the probate as evidence, but it is not decisive of ownership. The Court relied on Ishwardeo Narain Singh v. Smt. Kamta Devi and Chiranjilal Shrilal Goenka v. Jasjit Singh, and distinguished Rukmani Devi v. Narendra Lal Gupta as establishing the conclusiveness of probate as to the will, not as to title.

rule.if: appeal_from_dismissal_of_civil_title_suit_after_probate and probate_granted and plaint_claims_joint_family_ownership and title_claim_requires_evidence

predicates.appeal_from_dismissal_of_civil_title_sui: An appeal concerns dismissal of a civil suit for title and related relief after probate was granted.
predicates.probate_granted: A competent court granted probate of a will concerning the disputed property.
predicates.plaint_claims_joint_family_ownership: The plaintiff alleged that the disputed property belonged to a joint family rather than exclusively to the testator.
predicates.title_claim_requires_evidence: Resolving the ownership claim requires the parties to present evidence in the civil suit.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns dismissal of a civil title suit after probate, the plaintiff claims joint-family ownership, and resolving title requires evidence, the suit is not barred by probate.
